about: Phase 1C viability measurements (4-core Xeon 2.1 GHz, 15.7 GB RAM, no GPU). Cold = page cache dropped before starting the worker.

supertonic_fp32_onnx.download: ONNX graphs + unicode_indexer.json + tts.json + 10 voice styles (~0.3 MB each)
supertonic_fp32_onnx.streaming: No token streaming: non-autoregressive flow matching (8 steps) per text chunk (≤300 chars, sentence split); first audio = first chunk done.

supertonic_int8_sherpa_onnx.source: sherpa-onnx GitHub release tts-models/sherpa-onnx-supertonic-3-tts-int8-2026-05-11.tar.bz2 (INT8 by the sherpa-onnx/k2-fsa project, not by Supertone)

cold_start.note: process total includes 5 syntheses in that cold run

supertonic_int8_sherpa_onnx.note: INT8 is ~2.7× smaller and uses ~half the RAM, but on this x86 CPU it is slower than fp32 (RTF ~0.40 vs ~0.29).
supertonic_int8_sherpa_onnx.binding_bug: sherpa-onnx 1.13.8 Python: GenerationConfig.extra returns a copy, so the official example's `gen_config.extra['lang'] = …` is silently lost (language and seed never reach the engine). Assign the whole dict: gen_config.extra = {'lang': 'ru', 'seed': '…'}.

browser: Official: supertone-inc/supertonic web/ (onnxruntime-web; WebGPU with automatic WASM fallback; 'runs entirely in the browser'). Not executed here (no browser run). sherpa-onnx also publishes WebAssembly TTS builds.
android: No official Supertone Android sample (Flutter sample tested on macOS only; Java sample is desktop JVM; iOS/Swift samples are official). Credible route: sherpa-onnx (Apache-2.0), which ships Android/iOS/WASM builds and supports Supertonic 3 natively; the INT8 package measured here (~145 MB model, ~0.23–0.34 GB RSS on x86) is phone-sized.
offline: Fully offline once downloaded: no network calls in the ONNX runtimes (models are local files; ONNX Runtime only).

omnivoice.verdict: clearly impractical on this CPU (RTF ≈ 25) — stopped after Stage A
